name: manual_e93d89
claim: On Windows, never launch the long-lived stack (start.ps1) from an agent or app shell that sits in a job object: when breakaway is denied, spawn_detached falls back to launching inside the job, and the whole stack (PT, orama, Portal, TLS front end) dies when that app restarts. Check IsProcessInJob on the service launcher processes, not on the uvicorn children (the venv launcher holds those in its own job). Launch from outside the job (Task Scheduler at logon, a user terminal, or WMI Win32_Process.Create) and verify both peer directions after every restart, because one-way success hides a dead listener on the other side. Before each restart run git fetch origin main in each repository (remote-tracking refs only move on fetch), then move the run worktrees to origin/main so the stack runs the latest merged code, and confirm each listener's command line and bind address (Portal on IPv4 loopback, TLS front end on the LAN).

decisions.notes: 2026-11-04: Mac-to-Windows peer delivery timed out because nothing listened on the Windows TLS port. start.ps1 had been launched from an agent shell inside a desktop-app job object; spawn_detached's breakaway was denied, it fell back to launching inside the job, and an app restart killed PT, orama, Portal and the TLS front end together. Windows-to-Mac kept working because the Mac side runs under a persistent service manager, so the asymmetry went unnoticed. A later ad hoc portal bound IPv6 loopback only, and the run worktrees were 72-75 commits behind main, which produced a false LM Studio DOWN. Relaunching start.ps1 through WMI Win32_Process.Create put the service launchers outside any job (IsProcessInJob false); the uvicorn children stay only in their own venv-launcher job, which is expected.
